question: At 10 a.m. a company read news of a huge ore strike to reporters; a director then ordered shares. What did the appeals court rule?
options: Legal: he bought for family trusts
answer: Illegal: he jumped the gun. Texas Gulf Sulphur read its 1964 statement from 10:00 to about 10:15; it reached the Dow Jones news tape, which investors watched, at 10:54. In 1968 the appeals court held that reading news to reporters only starts it on its way: he should have waited at least for the tape.
move: News is public once people can act on it, not once it is spoken.
trap: ‘Legal: the news was out’: the trial judge had ruled just that.
simply: Shouting ‘free cake’ in one room does not make it fair to grab a slice before the people in the next room have heard.
why: It decides who may profit from a head start. Whoever hears news first, at work or on a board, can only profit by trading with people who could not yet know, which is why the law makes them wait.
